subject: Co-sell syndication and marketplace fallback runbook
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbus-sys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@aws-partners.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Co-sell syndication and marketplace fallback runbook

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this — excited to move Nimbus's listing into both AWS and GCP marketplaces and get the co-sell motion enabled. A couple of things we need clarity on from Redwood before we kick off the internal enablement at Nimbus: 

- Syndication model: we plan to list the same SKU across AWS and GCP. If the cloud marketplaces require different packaging or pricing metadata, what is Redwood's recommended approach to keep SKUs aligned for co-sell attribution?
- Fallback policy: if AWS Marketplace approves before GCP (or vice versa), can Redwood serve traffic across clouds while the other listing is pending? Any routing/fallback constraints we should plan for?
- Evidence: checklist of technical and go-to-market artifacts (publisher account IDs, telemetry proof, co-sell collateral) — can you share a recommended runbook we follow?

We'd like a short mutually-agreed timeline so our partnerships and legal teams can coordinate. Suggested window: listing approvals and co-sell enablement over the next 6 weeks.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Partnerships — Nimbus Systems
attachments: none listed (will share initial technical package after your reply)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbus-sys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-sell syndication and marketplace fallback runbook

Hi Sara — great to meet you virtually. Outline below and attaching our lightweight checklist to accelerate evidence collection.

Quick answers up front:
- Syndication & SKUs: we recommend a canonical SKU that lives in our control plane. For cloud listings we publish mapping metadata per marketplace (SKU mapping table) — that lets us keep unit economics consistent while satisfying each marketplace's catalog fields.
- Fallback servicing: Redwood can route inference requests to any region/cloud where we have capacity and the approved model variant. For marketplace billing attribution we rely on the listing's purchaser metadata; if one listing is not yet approved, we can still serve traffic from Redwood-hosted endpoints but co-sell attribution won't be retroactive. In practice we suggest: (a) do the first marketplace listing to completion, (b) enable cross-listing with SKU mapping, (c) use runtime routing for traffic while the second listing is pending, and (d) avoid counting co-sell credits until both listings have purchaser linkage.
- Evidence runbook: attaching redwood-syndication-checklist.pdf — it has publisher IDs, sample telemetry snippet, required SAML/OIDC metadata, and suggested co-sell collateral templates.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min kickoff this week to confirm timeline and responsibilities (we'll invite Ben for marketplace ops + Marissa for GTM collateral).
2) Nimbus uploads initial technical package to the Google Drive link in my follow-up.
3) We (Redwood) prepare the co-sell MOU draft and a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) spreadsheet for each marketplace.

Attached: redwood-syndication-checklist.pdf

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Partner Lead, Alliances — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-sell syndication and marketplace fallback runbook

Sofia — looping Alex on the technical checklist and ops questions. A few internal notes so we present a clear runbook on the kickoff call: 

- Marketplace packaging: Alex, confirm if current publishing pipeline supports per-marketplace SKU metadata and whether we need a minor release to support additional fields for GCP.
- Routing/serving: we support multi-cloud routing but need to validate any latency-sensitive customers — if Nimbus expects single-tenant performance SLAs in early trials, we should flag Dedicated capacity as an option.
- Attribution: legal needs the exact purchaser metadata fields we capture so they can confirm co-sell crediting language for the MOU. Marissa, can your GTM templates include a clause about "co-sell attribution contingent on purchaser metadata linkage"?

Alex — can you take the tech lead to detail the publishing steps (publisher account prep, certificates, telemetry sample) for the call? I'll draft the MAP (NIM-Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx) and share before the meeting.

Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Co-sell syndication and marketplace fallback runbook — kickoff confirmed

Hi Sara and team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming our kickoff and deliverables: 

Kickoff: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:00am PT — 30 minutes (Google Meet invite sent)
Deliverables before kickoff (Nimbus):
- Publisher account IDs for AWS and GCP (console account numbers)
- Initial listing metadata (canonical SKU, short/long descriptions, pricing tiers)
- Minimal telemetry sample (one week of aggregate request counts)

Deliverables from Redwood before next week:
- NIM-Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx (draft MAP) — attached to this thread
- redwood-syndication-checklist.pdf (attached previously)
- Draft co-sell MOU (DocuSign link will be provided post-call)

Notes on fallback: as discussed, Redwood will support serving while second listing is pending but co-sell credits and marketplace-specific incentives will only apply once purchaser linkage exists for that marketplace. If Nimbus requires co-sell-ready pricing earlier, please flag and we'll propose a limited pilot with Dedicated capacity.
